# TSR draft — refresh equipment model and serial from the edited schedule (1 batch)

**Status:** Executed locally 2026-10-18, not committed (on "Execute the TSR draft equipment refresh plan in
plans.md."). Approved 2026-10-18 ("Approved. Record it in plans.md."). One commit. Browser check also confirmed both
signatures survive a page reload plus the equipment refresh (owner asked); Review & Save TSR not run in the browser.

### Amendments during execution

- Step 2 moved: `applyStandaloneTSRDraftData` is also called by the online correction load (`:5418`), the late
  Calibration Report load (`:5710`) and the copy/version load (`:6696`), so calling the helper inside it would reach
  saved TSRs. The helper is called from `openStandaloneTSRDraft` instead, right after `applyStandaloneTSRDraftData`,
  with the live option matching `selectedStandaloneScheduleId`. The note is appended to the existing "Loaded saved TSR
  draft…" status (a separate `showTSRStatus` would be overwritten by it). The helper also returns early in
  `isOnlineTSRCalibrationMode()`. Test (2) checks `openStandaloneTSRDraft`, and that `applyStandaloneTSRDraftData` does
  not call the helper.

## Context

Owner scenario (2026-10-18): an engineer picks the wrong machine on a schedule, creates a TSR and saves a draft, then
corrects the schedule's equipment on Calendar. Reopening the draft still shows the old (wrong) Equipment Model and
Serial No. Both fields are locked on the Create TSR page, so the engineer cannot fix them there; the only workaround is
to re-pick the schedule. Intended outcome: reopening the draft shows the schedule's current equipment, and nothing else
the engineer typed changes.

## Decisions taken (owner, 2026-10-18)

- Reopening a draft refreshes Equipment Model and Serial No. from the live schedule (owner: "Plan a fix so reopening a
  TSR draft refreshes equipment model and serial from the edited schedule").
- Only those two fields. All other draft work (complaint, actions, parts, signatures, attachments, times, dates) stays
  as saved.

## Investigation (verified 2026-10-18, code read only)

- The draft is a frozen snapshot. Server copy: `TsrDraft.payload_json` (`app.py:3854–3875`); device copy: IndexedDB /
  localStorage. No schedule-edit route touches `TsrDraft` (every `TsrDraft.query` is in the draft routes,
  `app.py:18970–19602`).
- `applyStandaloneTSRDraftData` (`templates/offline_tsr.html:5254`) copies every `.tsr-field` from the draft (`:5265`),
  including `tsr-equipment-model` and `tsr-serial-no`. In the matched-schedule branch (`:5282–5285`) it only calls
  `syncStandaloneTSRAddressFromSchedule(matchedOption)`, which refreshes the address and the snapshot, nothing else
  (`:5237–5252`; guarded by `standaloneScheduleOptionsAreLive` and not revision mode).
- `renderSelectedStandaloneScheduleCard(matchedOption)` (`:5299`) then shows the live schedule card, so the card shows
  the new machine while the locked fields keep the old one.
- `openStandaloneTSRDraft` awaits `refreshStandaloneScheduleOptions(false)` before applying the draft (pinned by
  `tests/test_offline_resilience.py:491`), so live options exist when the matched branch runs online.
- A fresh pick fills the fields from the schedule: `applyScheduleToStandaloneTSR` sets `tsr-equipment-model` ←
  `schedule.product_name`, `tsr-serial-no` ← `schedule.product_id` (`:2746–2747`).
- Saving reads the form fields (`:3484`), so the TSR records whatever the fields show.
- `syncStandaloneTSRAddressFromSchedule` is also called on schedule refresh (`:2537`), the online correction load
  (`:5412`) and the late Calibration Report load for a saved TSR (`:5694`). Changing equipment there would touch saved
  TSRs, so that helper must stay address-only; existing tests pin it (`tests/test_offline_resilience.py:441–489`:
  no `setFieldValue(`, no `dispatchEvent(`, no save call in the helper).

## Execution steps

1. `templates/offline_tsr.html`: add `syncStandaloneTSREquipmentFromSchedule(schedule)` next to
   `syncStandaloneTSRAddressFromSchedule`. Same guards (return `false` unless `standaloneScheduleOptionsAreLive`, not
   `isOnlineTSRRevisionMode()`, and the schedule is the live matched option). If `schedule.product_name` is empty, do
   nothing (no-equipment schedules keep the draft's values). Otherwise set `tsr-equipment-model` ← `product_name` and
   `tsr-serial-no` ← `product_id` by direct `.value` assignment (no `setFieldValue`, no `dispatchEvent`, no save). Return
   `true` when either value changed. Done: helper exists, returns true only on a real change.
2. `applyStandaloneTSRDraftData`, matched branch only: call the new helper right after
   `syncStandaloneTSRAddressFromSchedule(matchedOption);`. When it returns `true`, after the `finally` block call
   `showTSRStatus('Equipment updated from the edited schedule. Check the Calibration Report if one was started.',
   'info')`. Done: the other three callers of the address helper are unchanged.
3. No change to the draft-list title/subtitle; they update on the next autosave or save.

## Deliberately excluded

- Calling the new helper on schedule refresh (`:2537`), online correction (`:5412`) or late Calibration Report
  (`:5694`): those touch saved TSRs or revision mode, where equipment changes go through the correction flow.
- Rewriting stored drafts on the server or device when a schedule is edited: drafts are never rewritten in bulk (comment
  at `:5271–5274`); the fix applies when the draft is opened.
- Resetting the Calibration Report when equipment changes: it may hold real work; the status message tells the engineer
  to check it.
- Offline reopen (cached options): `standaloneScheduleOptionsAreLive` is false, so the draft keeps its saved values, same
  as the address today.

## Verification

- New tests in `tests/test_offline_resilience.py`: (1) the new helper exists, has the live/revision guards, the empty
  `product_name` guard, assigns both field values, and has no `setFieldValue(`, `dispatchEvent(` or save call;
  (2) in `applyStandaloneTSRDraftData` the matched branch calls it after the address sync, and the `else if` /
  `else` branches do not; (3) the three other address-helper callers do not call it.
- Positive control: run the new tests in-process against `git show HEAD:templates/offline_tsr.html` (never
  `git stash`); each must fail there.
- Focused modules: `tests.test_offline_resilience`, `tests.test_tsr_draft_sync`. No full suite (one page only).
- Browser check on a copy of `scheduler.db` with an engineer test account: schedule with product A → Create TSR, type a
  complaint, save draft → edit the schedule to product B on Calendar → reopen the draft: model/serial show B, complaint
  kept, status message shown; reopen again with no change: no message; a no-equipment schedule draft keeps its values;
  Review & Save TSR records B. 375 px, console and server log clean. Clean up the DB copy, test account and launch
  entry.

## After implementation

- Self-review the diff; confirm `applyStandaloneTSRDraftData`, `openStandaloneTSRDraft`,
  `syncStandaloneTSRAddressFromSchedule`, `applyScheduleToStandaloneTSR`, save draft, Review & Save TSR, attachments
  and signatures still work, and no id or handler was removed.
- Prove the new tests fail without the fix, focused modules, browser check, service worker `CACHE_VERSION` bump in
  `app.py:28074` (v332 → v333), `static/changelog/releases.json` entry ("TSR drafts show the corrected equipment"),
  `changes.md`, Status here.
- On "commit and push": only `templates/offline_tsr.html`, `tests/test_offline_resilience.py`, `app.py` (SW bump),
  `static/changelog/releases.json`, `plans.md`, `changes.md`; never `scheduler.db`, `output/`, `tmp/`, handoffs or
  other dirty files. Verify `origin/main` and Railway deployment metadata.

## Risks

- A draft for a schedule whose equipment was changed on purpose to a different machine now shows the new one — that is
  the intended behaviour; the status message makes it visible.
- Blast radius: the Create TSR page's draft reopen only. Saved TSRs, corrections and late Calibration Reports are
  untouched (excluded callers, pinned by test 3).

# Genoray PM and Vieworks PM — scan and design-scan fixes (4 batches)

**Status:** Executed 2026-10-19 (on "Execute the Genoray/Vieworks PM plan in plans.md, all 4 batches."); not yet committed. Approved 2026-10-16 ("Write the 4 PM batches to plans.md as approved, then
wait."); amended the same day to include the detail page's sidebar highlight ("include the sidebar"). Each
batch is one commit. Start only on a separate go-ahead.

### Amendments during execution

- Step 5: the overview link is built in the page as `/${BRAND}/pm/<serial>` instead of `pm_url`, which resolves to the
  alias `/<brand>_pm/<serial>` that the sidebar highlight does not cover (noted under step 5).
- Step 13 caused two contrast drops on the page ground, both found and fixed in the browser check: the subtitle
  (`--app-muted` 4.41:1 in light → `--app-text`) and Bootstrap's grey outline header buttons (3.43–4.48:1 → themed
  `.pm-hero-actions .btn`, 12–16:1 text, border 4.35–9.7:1).
- Step 12: summary-card status shows as a coloured label in light (dark keeps the status colour pairs); the 5px green
  left border on history cards was removed too (same side-tab pattern).
- Results: 11 new tests (`tests/test_inventory_pm.py`: 4 route tests, 7 source tests); all 11 fail on `HEAD`
  (checked in a `git archive HEAD` copy, no stash). Focused modules 160/160. Full suite: 2122 tests, the known list plus
  two failures outside this change (`test_calibration_center` still expects `app-calibration-report.js?v=50`, bumped
  to 51 by `d5042fc`; `test_product_calibration_certificate` frozen-columns label changed by `fdded98`); `run_suite.py`
  needs `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` or it crashes printing a failure with a non-ASCII character.
- Browser check (DB copy, both brands): one POST on a double click; a linked visit moved to December is refused with
  "linked to schedule #879 in November…", unlink then succeeds; Escape closes the dialog and returns focus; errors stay;
  overview link opens the detail page with "Vieworks PM" highlighted and tab "Vieworks PM · Medical Service"; lowest text
  contrast 4.50:1 (white on the classic accent table header) in light, Graphite and AMOLED; 375 px: no horizontal
  scroll, no tap under 44px, visits start at 637px (was 1176px), editor last, phone bar "Inventory"; 700 px shows cards.

## Context

The owner moved on to the PM pages and asked for `/page-scan` and `/page-design-scan` of Genoray PM and Vieworks PM
(2026-10-16). Both pages are one template, `templates/inventory_pm.html`, and one set of routes (`/<brand>/pm`,
`/<brand>/pm/<serial>`, `/api/<brand>/pm/...`, `app.py:65267–65970`) with helpers at `app.py:4295–5207`, so every fix
lands on both brands. The design critique snapshot is
`.impeccable/critique/2026-10-16T07-32-32Z__templates-inventory-pm-html.md` (22/40, 2 × P1, degraded single-context run).
This list is closed (critique-loop rule): nothing is added during execution; anything new goes under "Amendments".

## Decisions taken (owner, 2026-10-16)

- Four batches, smallest first: server safety, page behaviour, dark mode and colours, layout.
- Vieworks plans keep their fixed one-year cycle (no warranty cutoff); that is intended (see the Genoray/Vieworks plan).
- A visit whose date moves out of its linked schedule's month is **refused** with a clear message (unlink, or pick a
  schedule in the new month), not silently unlinked.
- The detail page (`/<brand>/pm/<serial>`) gets its sidebar highlight too (owner: "include the sidebar", 2026-10-16).
  That is a `layout.html` change (shared code), so the full suite runs once before publishing.

## Investigation (verified 2026-10-16, browser check on a DB copy, admin and engineer test accounts)

Permissions: every page and API route checks `can_access_inventory_pm` (admin gate, `app.py:4557`); an engineer gets 403
on pages, GET, POST and DELETE (verified with a valid CSRF token). No server errors in the log; console errors were only
from the deliberate bad-input requests.

Logic findings:

1. **Medium · stale schedule link after a date move** — `inventory_pm_visit_api` (`app.py:65880–65887`) re-validates the
   link only when `shift_id` changes. The UI sends no `shift_id` when "Keep current schedule" is in effect
   (`inventory_pm.html:657`), so moving a visit from 2026-11-10 to 2026-12-10 kept schedule #879 (12 Nov). Reproduced:
   PUT `{target_date:'2026-12-10'}` → 200, `shift_id` 879, while December's options list is empty.
2. **Low · no date range** — `inventory_pm_target_date_from_payload` (`:65462`) and the POST `start_date` (`:65734`)
   accept any parseable date: POST `start_date: '0001-01-01'` created four visits in year 0001. The fiscal-year input
   already limits 1900–2200 (`app.py:4584`, `inventory_pm.html:216`).
3. **Low · Create Plan double submit** — `saveVisit` (`inventory_pm.html:637`) never disables the button; two quick
   clicks gave "Created 4 PM visits" and an error notice "All generated PM visit dates already exist". Data stays safe
   (date check + unique index). Same for Delete (`deleteVisit`, `:682`).
4. **Medium · overview is a dead end** — rows show the serial as text; `pm_url` is already in each item payload
   (`app.py:5133`) but no template uses it. The detail page is reachable only from the inventory pages' PM button.
5. **Low · "Filter by client" matches serial and name** — `visitMatchesFilters` (`:311–314`) uses the same haystack for
   search and client; typing a serial in the client box kept 2 of 2 visits.
6. **Low · wording** — subtitle says "showing N of M planned visits" (`:360`) while counting Completed and Overdue too.
7. **Low · detail page has no sidebar highlight and a generic tab title** — `nav_link` marks a link active only on an
   exact path match (`layout.html:140`), so `/<brand>/pm/<serial>` has no `aria-current` link, and the layout script
   that names the tab and the phone top bar from that link (`layout.html:505–516`) leaves "Medical Service". The page's
   own `<title>` in `page_head` (`inventory_pm.html:4`) is a second `<title>` after layout's (`layout.html:48`) and is
   ignored.
8. **Low · speed** — `inventory_pm_visit_to_dict` (`app.py:4950`) loads each linked Shift twice (`db.session.get` then the
   same query with options, `:4955–4965`) and runs `inventory_pm_rebuild_metadata` (one plan query per visit, `:5116`)
   even for the overview, which never reads `cadence_rebuild` (only `updateEditCadenceState`, `inventory_pm.html:494`,
   on the detail page).
9. **Simplify** — `decorateVisit` / `itemBySerial` (`inventory_pm.html:317–324`) rebuild `item_name` and `client_name`
   that the server already sends in each visit (`app.py:5077–5079`), with a linear search per visit, twice per render.

Not findings: cadence rebuild is atomic and blocked for linked or completed visits; completed history is immutable
(409); purge is blocked while PM visits exist; serial renames carry PM visits; HTML is escaped; 375 px has no horizontal
scroll and no tap target under 44 px.

Design findings (measured, light / Graphite / AMOLED):

10. **P1 · dark mode** — overview count numbers `.pm-summary-card strong` `#0f172a` on `#292a2d` = **1.24:1** (Graphite);
    `.pm-summary-card span`, `.pm-state`, `.pm-month-heading span` `#64748b` = 3.02:1 Graphite, 4.0:1 AMOLED; editor
    eyebrow `#0f766e` = 2.62:1; visit cards, equipment fields and the confirm dialog stay white `#fff`/`#f8fafc` on the
    dark page. Cause: hex colours in the page `<style>` (`inventory_pm.html:735–787`; detector: 25 design-system-color).
11. **P2 · off-system colours** — table headers `#0f3d56` and the gradient hero ignore `--app-primary` (DESIGN "Don't
    hardcode an accent hex"); status chips `#b91c1c/#fee2e2` (Overdue), `#047857/#d1fae5` (Completed) differ from the
    documented semantic pairs (`#a1121f/#fde8ea`, `#166534/#dcfce7`, DESIGN "Inventory status"); summary cards use a
    5px left border on a 16px radius (detector: 3 × side-tab); radii 13px and 15px (DESIGN: cards 10–12, phone 16);
    weights 750–950 (DESIGN: above 600 renders as 600).
12. **P2 · ≤768 px rule** — at 621–768 px the 1100px-min table shows (horizontal scroll) instead of cards (DESIGN
    Layout: tables become stacked cards at ≤768); the switch is at 620 px (`:785`).
13. **P2 · phone order** — at 375 px the hero is 188px tall and the planned visits start at 1176px, below the equipment
    card and the whole editor.
14. **P3 · dialog and notices** — `pmConfirm` (`:235`) has no Escape and does not return focus; error notices remove
    themselves after 7 s (`:232`).

## Execution steps

### Batch 1 — server safety and speed (`app.py` only)

1. `inventory_pm_visit_api` (`app.py:65880`): when no link field is sent, `visit.shift_id` is set and the new
   `target_date` is in a different calendar month than the current `target_date`, run
   `validate_inventory_pm_schedule_link(item, visit.shift_id, target_date)`; on error return 400 with "This visit is
   linked to schedule #N in <Month>. Unlink it or choose a schedule in the new month." Done: the reproduction above
   returns 400; a same-month date change still returns 200.
2. Date range: in `inventory_pm_target_date_from_payload` and the POST `start_date` path, refuse dates outside
   1900-01-01–2200-12-31 with "Target date must be between 1900 and 2200." Done: year 0001 → 400, nothing created.
3. `inventory_pm_visit_to_dict`: replace the `db.session.get` + re-query pair with the single options query; add
   `include_rebuild=True` and pass `False` from `inventory_pm_overview_payload` and the GET list in
   `inventory_pm_visits_api` (key `cadence_rebuild` becomes `None` there). Done: detail payload unchanged; overview
   output identical apart from `cadence_rebuild`.

### Batch 2 — page behaviour (`templates/inventory_pm.html` script)

4. `saveVisit` / `deleteVisit`: disable the Save button (and the clicked Delete) while the request runs; re-enable in
   `finally`. Done: two quick clicks send one POST.
5. Overview: the serial in the table row and phone card links to the item's `pm_url` (from `data.items`); fall back to
   text when absent. Done: clicking opens `/<brand>/pm/<serial>`.
   *Amended during execution:* `pm_url` resolves to the alias route `/<brand>_pm/<serial>` (seen in the browser check),
   which the sidebar highlight does not cover, so the link is built in the page as `/${BRAND}/pm/<serial>` for serials
   present in `data.items`, the same way `products.html` builds its PM link (`inventoryPMBaseUrl`, `:1488`).
6. `visitMatchesFilters`: client box matches `client_name` only. Subtitle: "showing N of M visits".
7. Remove `decorateVisit` / `itemBySerial` and use the server's `item_name` / `client_name` (keep `pm_url` lookup from a
   serial → item map built once per render). Grep first: no other caller.
8. `pmConfirm`: Escape cancels, focus returns to the button that opened it. Error notices stay until dismissed (success
   notices keep 4 s).
9. Sidebar highlight and tab title: in `nav_link` (`layout.html:140`) also treat a link as active when its `href` is
   `/genoray/pm` or `/vieworks/pm` and `request.path` starts with `href ~ '/'` (PM hrefs only; every other link keeps
   the exact match). The existing title script then names the tab "Genoray PM · Medical Service" / "Vieworks PM · …"
   and the phone top bar shows Inventory. Drop the ignored `<title>` from `inventory_pm.html` `page_head`. Done: the
   detail page has exactly one `aria-current="page"` link (Genoray PM or Vieworks PM), `/genoray` and `/vieworks` stay
   inactive on PM pages, and no other page's highlight changes.

### Batch 3 — dark mode and colours (page `<style>`; DESIGN.md)

10. Replace hex text and surface colours with tokens: text `var(--app-text)`, muted `var(--app-muted)`, cards and field
    boxes `var(--app-surface)` / `var(--app-surface-raised)`, borders `var(--app-border)`; editor eyebrow
    `var(--app-primary-text)`; table header `var(--app-primary)` with white text; confirm dialog and notices on
    `var(--app-surface)`. Done: every measured element ≥4.5:1 in light, Graphite and AMOLED.
11. Status chips: Overdue `#a1121f/#fde8ea`, Completed `#166534/#dcfce7`, Planned keeps `#1d4ed8/#dbeafe`; dark pairs as
    Inventory status (`#fecdd3/#5c1a22`, `#bbf7d0/#14532d`) plus Planned `#bfdbfe/#1e3a8a`. Record the PM pairs in
    DESIGN.md "Chips / Badges".
12. Summary cards: remove the 5px left border; status shown by the label colour only paired with its text. Radii 13→12,
    15→16; weights above 600 → 600.

### Batch 4 — layout (page markup and `<style>`)

13. Replace the gradient hero with a plain page header on the page surface: Bootstrap heading, one-line subtitle, the
    existing outline buttons (keep `#pm-print-btn`, the back/inventory link and all ids). Print styles stay white.
14. Move the table → card switch from 620 px to 768 px (`.pm-table-wrap` hidden, `.pm-mobile-visits` shown).
15. Detail page at ≤768 px: show "Planned visits" and "PM History" before the editor (CSS `order` on a flex column
    wrapper); desktop order unchanged.

## Deliberately excluded

- Listing equipment that has no PM plan in the overview: a new feature, not a fix.
- Removing the server-side overview filters (`inventory_pm_filtered_overview_payload`) and the route/response aliases:
  tests use `?scheduled_month=` (`tests/test_inventory_pm.py:405`) and aliases may be used by bookmarks; no gain worth
  the risk.
- Vieworks warranty cutoff: intended (Decisions).

## Verification

- New tests in `tests/test_inventory_pm.py`: (1) month-changing PUT on a linked visit → 400, same-month → 200;
  (2) POST and PUT with year 0001 → 400 and no rows; (3) overview visits carry `cadence_rebuild is None`, detail visits
  keep it. New source tests for the template (pattern of `tests/test_dashboard_critique_fixes.py`): Save disabled
  during request, `pm_url` link rendered, client filter uses `client_name`, Escape handler, no `#0f172a`/`#64748b` in
  the PM `<style>`, card switch at 768px, no `<title>` in `page_head`. In `tests/test_layout_sidebar.py`: rendering
  `/genoray/pm/<serial>` and `/vieworks/pm/<serial>` marks only the matching PM link `aria-current="page"`; `/genoray`
  and `/products_page` keep their exact-match highlight.
- Positive control: run each new test in-process against `git show HEAD:app.py` / `HEAD:templates/inventory_pm.html`
  (never `git stash`); each must fail there.
- Focused modules: `tests.test_inventory_pm`, `tests.test_genoray_inventory`, `tests.test_vieworks_inventory`,
  `tests.test_operational_equipment_workflows`, `tests.test_dashboard_critique_fixes`, `tests.test_layout_sidebar`.
  Full suite once before publishing (`layout.html` is shared), from the main project folder.
- Browser check on a DB copy (both brands): create plan, double-click, edit date in and out of month with a linked
  schedule, unlink, delete with Escape and Continue, overview link to detail, filters, sidebar highlight and tab title on both detail pages (desktop rail, pinned
  sidebar and phone top bar); contrast re-measured in light,
  Graphite and AMOLED; 375 px and 700 px (cards, no horizontal scroll, taps ≥44px); console and server log clean.
- Re-check the critique's closed list item by item; one fresh critique in a new session afterwards, not a loop.

## After implementation

- Self-review the diff; confirm `loadOverview`, `renderOverview`, `loadDetail`, `saveVisit`, `deleteVisit`,
  `startVisitEdit`, `resetVisitForm`, `loadScheduleOptions`, `previewRecurringPlan`, `updateEditCadenceState`, Print,

- Prove the new tests fail without the fix, focused modules, browser check, service worker `CACHE_VERSION` bump,

## Risks

# TSR without equipment — update two tests to the User roles rule (1 batch, tests only)

**Status:** Executed (2026-10-16, on "commit and push together", taken as the go-ahead). Published to `main` as `73315f9`
with the Genoray/Vieworks fixes. Approved 2026-10-16
("Approved. Write the TSR-without-equipment test fix to plans.md and wait.").

### Amendments during execution

  `can_create_tsr_without_equipment_for_user` each makes `test_default_off_and_effective_permission_follows_switch` fail.

## Context

Two tests in `tests/test_tsr_without_equipment.py` fail on `main` and are not in `tests/known_failures.txt`. The Genoray
and Vieworks session found them during its focused run. They began failing with `4ab0627` (User roles), which
deliberately removed the "Francis only" username rule. The tests still expect that rule.

  roles plan, step 15: "drop the username check … grant works for a non-Francis engineer and is refused for staff").

  profile and the account switch — no username.

   with the switch on). Done = test passes and still fails if the role or profile check is removed.

## Context

The 2026-10-16 page scan and design scan of `templates/products.html` in Genoray (`/genoray`) and Vieworks (`/vieworks`)
mode, the follow-up to the Product Inventory plan below (published `99719b6`). Critique snapshot:
`.impeccable/critique/2026-10-16T00-00-00Z__templates-products-html-genoray-vieworks.md` (27/40, only what differs from
product mode). The worst problems: a Vieworks CSV import can move a linked item to a different medical center than its
machine; both imports still erase owner, dates and room when a column is missing (the bug fixed for products on
2026-10-15); the list API makes one calibration query per row; the PM button is unreadable in dark themes.

## Decisions taken (owner, 2026-10-16)

- All four batches go into this plan, as proposed after the scan.
- Follow the Product Inventory fixes already published wherever the same bug exists here (import column rule, "N/A"
  owner, fuzzy-match count, delete of a missing row → 404), so the three inventories behave the same.

## Investigation

- **Vieworks import breaks the machine link** (`import_vieworks_items`, `app.py:66130`): for an existing item it sets
  `existing.client_id = client_id` with no link check, while `update_vieworks_item` (`app.py:65955`) rejects a client that
  differs from the linked Product's ("A linked Vieworks/Canon item must remain with the same medical center as its
  Product."). Repro on a DB copy: VW-SCAN-1 linked to MPF16817600 (client 7); importing `VW-SCAN-1,VW Scan,"Accura-Tech
  Diagnostic Laboratory"` → "1 updated", item now at Accura-Tech, `linked_product` still the client-7 machine. The next
  Edit then drops the link without a word (the Linked Machine list only offers the new center's machines,
  `refreshProductLinkOptions`, `products.html:1224`).
- **Both imports erase missing columns** (`import_vieworks_items` and `import_genoray_items`, `app.py:66498`): an
  existing row always gets `room`, `client_id`, `start_warranty_date`, `end_warranty_date` from the CSV, even when the
  column is absent. `import_products` (`app.py:66853`, `has_room_column` … `has_bsid_column` at `:66879`) already uses
  the "only change what the CSV carries" rule.
- **"N/A" owner on re-import**: export writes `N/A` for no owner (`export_vieworks_items` `app.py:66255`,
  `export_genoray_items` `:66622`); re-importing that export reports "1 owner name(s) were not matched" (seen in the
  browser on Genoray). `import_products` treats "N/A" as empty and counts fuzzy matches through
  `csv_find_client_match` (`app.py:66689`, returns `(client_id, exact)`); the brand imports call the old
  `csv_find_client_id` and apply fuzzy matches silently.
- **Delete of a missing serial** returns 200 `success` in `delete_vieworks_item` (`app.py:66098`) and
  `delete_genoray_item` (`:66468`); `delete_product` returns 404 "Product not found." since `99719b6`.
- **N+1 list queries**: `get_genoray_items` (`app.py:35274`) and `get_vieworks_items` (`:35117`) call
  `genoray_item_to_dict` / `vieworks_item_to_dict` (`:34886`, `:34958`) per row; each runs
  `latest_approved_calibration_approvals_for_equipment([(item, source)])` (one joined query per row) and lazy-loads
  `owner`; Vieworks also runs `product_vieworks_parent_payload` (`:3197`: link query + item lookups + Product get) per
  row. `get_products` already batches both (`:34845` `product_vieworks_link_payload_map`, `:34852` one calibration call).
  The Add/PUT responses also call the `*_to_dict` twice (`'item': …, **…`).
- **Dead code**: `role = …` assigned and never used in `can_access_genoray_inventory` (`app.py:8602`) and
  `can_access_vieworks_inventory` (`:8683`).
- **Serial change text is wrong for brand modes**: the help text says only "This will create an activity log."
  (`openEditModal`, `products.html:2070`) and the confirm says "The change will be recorded in Activity Logs."
  (`saveProduct`, `:2180`), but the PUT routes move the item's schedules and PM visits (`app.py` `update_vieworks_item`
  `Shift … update`, `InventoryPmVisit … update`; same in `update_genoray_item`) and return `linked_schedule_count` /
  `pm_visit_count`, which the page ignores.
- **Labels**: count line "Showing 2 of 2 genoray items" / "0 of 0 vieworks items" (`products.html:1410`, `:1416`,
  `:1414-1415` use `inventoryPlural.toLowerCase()`); history subtitle "genoray · SN" while loading (`openProductHistory`,
  `:1731`, raw `source`); table header "Product Name" (`:172`) and search placeholder "S/N or Product Name" (`:96`) while
  the modal says "Genoray/Vieworks Equipment Name".
- **Delete has no success message** (`deleteProduct`, `:2278-2282`), while Add and Edit toast. All three modes.
- **Simplify**: `openAddModal` sets `bsidField.disabled = isGenorayInventory;` then `if(isVieworksInventory) … = true`
  (`:2034-2035`) — one line `= isStandaloneInventory`.
- **PM button contrast** (brand modes only; measured with transitions disabled): phone `.product-mobile-pm`
  (`products.html:3288`, `#115e59` on `#ccfbf1`) becomes link blue `#6ea8fe` on the same light teal in dark themes:
  2.14:1 Graphite and AMOLED (light 5.92). Desktop `.product-row-pm` icon (`:2785`) 2.32:1 Graphite/AMOLED (light 6.40;
  non-text needs ≥3:1).
- **Vieworks rows never show their machine**: `renderProductLinkedVieworks` (`:1466`) returns `''` in brand modes; the
  data (`linked_product`) is already loaded but only appears in Service History and the Edit list. Product rows do show
  their linked Vieworks.
- **Empty state** "No Vieworks items available." (`:1035`, `:1049`) offers no next step, though Add and Import exist.
- **Not a finding**: Vieworks PM plans have no warranty cutoff on purpose (`cutoff = … if normalized == 'genoray'`,
  `app.py:65502`, `:65664`), so `update_vieworks_item` not calling a PM repair is correct. Server validation (BSID clear,
  lengths, dates, unknown client) is in `genoray_payload_values` / `vieworks_payload_values` (`:35390`, `:35480`).
  Permissions are enforced on every route (edit: `can_edit_*`; delete/import/PM: `can_administer_*`). No console or
  server errors; 375px has no horizontal scroll and no tap under 44px; HTML in names is escaped.

## Execution steps

### Batch 1 — imports, delete, list speed (`app.py`)

1. `import_vieworks_items`: for an existing item that has a `ProductVieworksLink`, if the CSV owner column is present and
   resolves to a different client than the linked Product's, skip the row and count it in a new `link_conflicts` field;
   message adds "N row(s) skipped: a linked Vieworks item must stay with its machine's medical center." Done = repro above
   leaves the item at client 7 and reports 1 conflict.
2. Both imports: change `room`, `client_id`, start and end date of an existing row only when the CSV has that column
   (copy the `has_*_column` checks from `import_products`, `app.py:66879`). New rows unchanged. Done = CSV with only
   Serial + Description keeps owner, dates and room.
3. Both imports: treat owner "N/A" (any case) as empty; use `csv_find_client_match` and report `fuzzy_owner_matches` plus
   "N owner name(s) were matched approximately — check them." exactly as `import_products` does. Done = re-importing an
   export reports 0 unmatched owners.
4. `delete_vieworks_item` / `delete_genoray_item`: 404 `{'message': 'Vieworks item not found.'}` / `'Genoray item not
   found.'` when the serial does not exist.
5. List speed: `genoray_item_to_dict(item, calibration_approval=_MISSING)` and `vieworks_item_to_dict(item,
   calibration_approval=_MISSING, linked_product=_MISSING)` accept precomputed values (fall back to today's per-item
   lookups when not given, so other callers keep working). `get_genoray_items` / `get_vieworks_items` load rows with
   `joinedload(owner)`, make one `latest_approved_calibration_approvals_for_equipment` call for all rows, and (Vieworks)
   one new `product_vieworks_parent_payload_map(serials)` built like `product_vieworks_link_payload_map` (`app.py:3167`),
   same payload shape as `product_vieworks_parent_payload`. Add/PUT responses build the dict once. Done = list JSON
   identical before/after on the DB copy; query count no longer grows with rows.
6. Remove the unused `role = …` lines in `can_access_genoray_inventory` and `can_access_vieworks_inventory`.

### Batch 3 — PM button contrast (`templates/products.html` page CSS)

# User roles — no hardcoded usernames, role dropdown in Settings, Support Engineer role (4 batches)

**Status:** Executed — published to `main` as `4ab0627` on 2026-10-16 ("Commit and push the User roles change"; owner
took a fresh database backup first). All four batches in one commit (they share `app.py`/template hunks).
**Approved:** 2026-10-15 — the owner said "Approved. Write the four-batch roles plan to plans.md." Under the two-step
rule this records approval only; execution needs a separate instruction.
**Origin:** 2026-10-15 page scan of the Settings → Users tab (role focus), then owner decisions in the same session.
Four batches, one commit each, published together or one at a time on "commit and push".

### Amendments during execution

- **Production never ran `migrate_hierarchy_accounts`.** Gunicorn (`RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT`) only runs
  `prepare_deferred_workflow_schemas()` at import and the per-request `ensure_runtime_sqlite_migrations_before_request`;
  `initialize_database()` is `__main__`-only. The one-time migrations therefore run from that per-request hook (once per
  process, via `run_role_migrations()`) and from `initialize_database()`. Markers in `app_migration`: `roles_v1`,
  `roles_v2_protected_account`, `roles_v3_default_approver`; the marker row is inserted first so a second gunicorn worker's
  claim fails instead of re-running.
- **`diary` already resolved to the Diary Dizon profile** through the `engineer_profile` name-prefix fallback, so moving
  the link changed nothing in her snapshot (no new engineer items).
- **Owned-records check** also counts integer `created_by`/`updated_by` columns (`purchase_order`,
  `reimbursement_tracker_*`), not only `*user_id`/`*_by_id` and user FKs.
- **Legacy role `'admin'` kept in the three inventory-admin helpers** (`can_administer_products_inventory`, Genoray,
  Vieworks): no production account holds it, but 80+ inventory test fixtures use it. Removed everywhere else.
- **Batch 3 approval queues:** one explained difference. Rodito's own requests (id 1) leave his own queue — routing never
  lets a requester approve himself; they already route to Anthony. Anthony's only route to Rodito had been deactivated,
  so he reached an approver only through the name bypass; the v3 migration reactivated that route (production log line
  `[Roles] Routed 'anthony' to the default approver.`). All other queues identical.
- **Support Engineer writes are gated in one place** — `restrict_support_engineer_writes()` (`before_request`) over
  `SUPPORT_ENGINEER_DENIED_ENDPOINTS` (TSR/calibration writes, schedule writes, Cash Advance) — instead of a check in each
  of ~25 routes. Products go through `can_manage_supported_inventory_as_engineer`; Create TSR and drafts through
  `can_back_up_tsr_drafts` → `can_do_field_work`; new travel requests are refused inside `save_travel_request_draft`.
  Existing TSR/schedule write routes that already required `role == 'engineer'` were left as they are (they exclude
  Support Engineers already). The travel page shows a notice above the form rather than replacing it, so requests the
  Support Engineer is on still open there. Timeline uses the existing read-only mode with a "Support Engineer View" banner.
- **`nav_rights_role`** (context processor) is what page scripts compare against: `superadmin` for the superadmin family,
  `regional_admin`, `engineer` for Support Engineers, else the raw role. Replaces `current_user.role` in timeline,
  engineers, clients.
- **Role dropdown** also refuses a scheduler changing an admin account or giving an admin role (same limit as admin
  delete), and `approver` without Can Approve.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_roles_from_database.py` (15 tests; all fail on `HEAD`, run from a `git archive` export). 27 test
  files updated from name lists to roles; tests whose premise was "superadmin role without the name list has no rights"
  now use a `staff` account.

## Context

The owner wants to change a user's role from Settings and add a new **Support Engineer** role. Today that cannot work:
rights come from **usernames**, not from `User.role`. Superadmin, manager, scheduler and regional-admin authority are
fixed username lists (`app.py:8137-8165`), `migrate_hierarchy_accounts` forces six named accounts back to their roles on
every start (`app.py:67052`), and the timeline repeats the names in JavaScript. The owner's rules for the rework: **no
hardcoded username rules, no change to what each role may do, nobody loses any access in production**, and clean up
the two stray logins `hannah` and `diarydizon`.

## Decisions taken (owner, 2026-10-15)

1. **Roles become the only source of truth.** New role values `manager` and `scheduler` hold exactly today's
   Manager/Scheduler rights. Superadmin, Manager and Scheduler are all "superadmin family" (today's
   `is_superadmin_user()` rights); Scheduler keeps its narrower password-reset and admin-delete limits; Regional Admin
   keeps Cebu/Davao-only by role.
2. **Approvals = Approval Routing only.** Remove Rodito's username rules (sees everything, six name fallbacks,
   auto re-added routes). New per-account **Default approver** checkbox; new accounts are routed to the ticked
   default approver(s) when they are created. A route the owner removes stays removed.
3. **Protected developer account** — one per-account checkbox replacing the `jonamar` name rules: password cannot be
   reset/deactivated/deleted by anyone else, engineer-only dashboard, timeline developer view picker. Only a protected
   account may untick it.
4. **Francis grant** ("Create TSR without assigned equipment") becomes checkbox-only: any active engineer-type
   account with an Engineer profile can be ticked; the username lock goes.
5. **Support Engineer** (`support_engineer`, label "Support Engineer") is a **view-only** engineer. Same as Engineer
   for reimbursements, leave, dashboard, Personnel and viewing pages, except:
   - **Products:** can view; cannot add, edit or delete — Product, Genoray and Vieworks lists (one helper governs all
     three; assumption stated to owner).
   - **Schedules:** can view and can be assigned by admins; cannot add, edit or delete schedules, including their own,
     and cannot change status or upload files on an assigned schedule (owner, 2026-10-15: "they cant add/edit/delete
     schedules even submit tsr or calibration").
   - **TSR and calibration:** cannot create, draft, submit, revise or upload a TSR, cannot save or submit a calibration
     report or certificate, cannot email a TSR to the client, cannot add knowledge-base entries. They can still view
     TSRs (archive, history) and calibration reports they may see today.
   - **Travel requests:** cannot create one. As a participant on someone else's request they need no saved signature
     (a saved one still prints). They can still open requests they are on, as any participant can today.
   - **Cash advance:** no access (page, save, submit, liquidation creation), link hidden.
   - Owner sets who gets the role through the new dropdown after release; no account is migrated to it.
6. **Stray logins.** `diarydizon`'s Personnel row "Diary Dizon" (12-139) moves to the real `diary` login, then
   `diarydizon` is deleted; `hannah` is deleted. Expected consequence accepted by the owner: `diary` gains engineer
   tools (own timeline row, signature, TSRs) and the scheduler + engineer dashboard Hanna already has.
7. **Production safety:** nobody loses access. Proven with a before/after access snapshot on a copy of production
   (below); any unexplained difference blocks the publish. Fresh backup before the push.

## Risks

- **Lost access in production** — the main risk. Safety net: the access snapshot on a production copy, the full suite,
  migrations that only add columns and run once, and a fresh backup.
- **Rollback:** reverting the code is safe — old code's `migrate_hierarchy_accounts` puts rodito/diary/hanna back to
  `superadmin` on start and ignores new columns and the `app_migration` table. Deleted logins (`hannah`,
  `diarydizon`) and the moved Personnel link are restored only from the backup.
- **Dead role values becoming live** (`'manager'`, `'scheduler'` literals) — each reviewed in step 5 and covered by
  the snapshot.
- **Diary's dashboard changes** (accepted by the owner) — she gains engineer sections and her schedule rows.
- **Blast radius:** login/permission helpers used by every page, Settings, timeline, Personnel, approvals, products,
  travel, cash advance. One commit per batch so a batch can be reverted alone.

# Calibration Report on a revised TSR — move it to the latest revision instead of "belongs to another TSR" (1 batch)

**Status:** Executed (2026-10-15, on "Execute the revised-TSR calibration report plan."). Published on "commit and
push. never db and dirty" as `47de227` on `main`. One batch, one commit, server-side only.

### Amendments during execution

- **Helper return value:** `relink_calibration_report_to_latest_revision` returns `'moved'`, `'approved'` or `''`
  (not True/False), so the route can tell "approved on the older revision" apart from "not this case".
- **One call site:** the helper runs in the early token check of `upload_online_tsr_attachment` and the route commits
  right after a move; the later check inside the existing-file branch (`app.py` ~27176) then sees the file on the
  latest revision and needs no change. If a later step of that request fails, the file stays on the latest revision
  and the next retry continues from there.
- **Older Pending certificate → Superseded** is not asserted in the new tests (they patch
  `submit_calibration_certificate_for_submission`); it is existing behaviour of that function. The tests assert the
  certificate is sent for the latest revision.
- **Fail-without-fix proof:** before the change, the two "moves to latest revision" tests failed with exactly the
  engineer's error (409 "This attachment token belongs to another TSR.") and the approved test got no `error_code`;
  the different-TSR test is a coverage test and passes on both.
- **Browser (DB copy, test engineer):** uploaded a report on TSR 35 (REV1), created REV2 the way a revision does
  (same report, REV1 superseded), opened REV2's calibration page and pressed Save Final Report: upload 200 with the
  same token, report file moved to REV2, REV2 listed on My Calibrations ("Failed to send: Missing values: Certificate
  No." — the copy's test machine has no BSID). No page file changed, so no service worker bump.
- **Correction to the retry plan's note:** "a My Calibrations read right after an upload did not list the new row" was
  a test-login slip (the browser was signed in as another user), not app behaviour; signed in as the right engineer the
  row is listed at once.

## Context

After the weak-signal saves (see the two Late Calibration Report plans below), the engineer now gets "This attachment
token belongs to another TSR." on Save Final Report, with a working connection. The Calibration Report upload token is
a fingerprint of the report's content only, not of the TSR. A TSR revision is a new `OnlineTsrSubmission` row, and the
browser re-uploads the same report with the same token; the older revision already owns a `ShiftFile` with that token,
so the server refuses it. Result: the revised TSR has no report, My Calibrations (latest revision only) shows nothing,
and every retry fails the same way. Intended outcome: the report follows the TSR to its latest revision and its
certificate is sent, while a token owned by a genuinely different TSR is still refused.

## Decisions taken (owner, 2026-10-15)

- Fix on the server: move the report to the latest revision of the same TSR instead of refusing.
- Keep the content-based token (no per-revision token).
- One batch. Do not disturb other plans in this file (the Product Inventory plan below was added by another session).

## Investigation

- Token = `'calibration-report-' + fingerprint(report)` (`static/js/app-calibration-report.js:1594`); nothing ties it
  to a submission.
- `revise_online_tsr_submission` (`app.py:27460`) creates a new submission (`mark_existing_online_tsr_submissions_superseded`
  then `OnlineTsrSubmission(..., is_latest=True)`) and links only files sent with that request
  (`attach_uploaded_online_tsr_extra_files_to_shift`); the old report file stays on the old revision. The browser then
  calls `uploadTSRSupportingAttachments` (`templates/offline_tsr.html:9112`), which re-uploads every attachment,
  including the generated report with the same token.
- `upload_online_tsr_attachment` refuses any token whose `ShiftFile` is linked to another submission — early at
  `app.py:27076` and again inside the existing-file branch (`app.py:27176`). Both return
  "This attachment token belongs to another TSR." (409).
- The file must be moved, not just reused: `calibration_certificate_generated_report_source_file` (`app.py:24700`)
  requires `report_file.online_tsr_submission_id == approval.online_tsr_submission_id`, and
  `calibration_report_pdf_file_for_source` requires the ready PDF's `online_tsr_submission_id` to equal the source's.
- Sending the certificate for the new revision already closes older ones for the same shift
  (`submit_calibration_certificate_for_submission`, `app.py:26523`: older `is_latest` → False, `Pending` → `Superseded`).
- The local `scheduler.db` copy (data to 2026-10-14) has no such case; the engineer's TSR was not inspected (no
  production access). The cause is confirmed in code, not in the engineer's data.

## Execution steps

1. **Helper** in `app.py`, next to `record_calibration_report_upload`:
   `relink_calibration_report_to_latest_revision(existing_file, submission)` → True only when all hold: the file is a
   generated Calibration Report source (`calibration_report_source_file_is_private` / DOCX name); same `shift_id`; the
   owning submission is an older revision of that shift (`is_latest` False, different id) and `submission.is_latest`
   is True; the owning revision's latest certificate approval is not `Approved`. Then set
   `existing_file.online_tsr_submission_id = submission.id` and, when the conversion job has a PDF
   (`calibration_report_conversion_for_source(existing_file.id).pdf_shift_file_id`), the PDF's too. Otherwise False with
   no change. Done: unit-testable, no commit inside (caller commits).
2. **Use it in both checks** of `upload_online_tsr_attachment` (`app.py:27076`, `:27176`), only when
   `attachment_source == 'generated_calibration_report'`: if the helper moved the file, continue down the existing-file
   branch (record the marker on the latest revision via `record_calibration_report_upload`, schedule conversion, submit
   the certificate, return success with `duplicate: true`). Done: older-revision tokens of the same TSR succeed; other
   TSRs still get 409.
3. **Approved on the older revision:** when the only blocker is an `Approved` certificate on the older revision, return
   409 with `error_code: 'calibration_report_approved_on_earlier_revision'` and the message "This Calibration Report was
   approved on an earlier revision of this TSR and cannot be moved." Nothing moves.
4. **Release:** `static/changelog/releases.json` item; service worker bump only if a page file changes (expected not);
   `changes.md`; this plan's Status.

## Deliberately excluded

- Per-revision upload tokens: would also avoid the clash, but changes how retries are recognised and affects reports
  already saved on devices; moving within the same TSR is smaller.
- Moving a report whose certificate was approved on an older revision: stays put with a clear message; whether an
  approved report should follow a revision is a separate decision.
- Tokens owned by a genuinely different TSR (different shift): still refused.
- Revisions saved on a device that no longer has the report file (missing blob): separate issue.

## Verification

- New tests in `tests/test_calibration_late_upload_feedback.py`:
  - REV1 owns the report file (+ ready PDF via a conversion job), REV2 is latest: late upload and ordinary
    attachment-path upload to REV2 succeed; file and PDF now linked to REV2; certificate sent for REV2; REV1's
    `Pending` approval becomes `Superseded`; My Calibrations lists REV2.
  - File owned by a different shift: still 409 "belongs to another TSR".
  - REV1 certificate `Approved`: 409 with the new message; nothing moved.
- Positive control: the new tests fail on the current code.
- Focused modules: `test_calibration_late_upload_feedback`, `test_tsr_sync_reliability`, `test_my_calibrations`,
  `test_calibration_report_returned_fix`, `test_calibration_certificate_approval_workflow`,
  `test_calibration_report_page`, `test_changelog_coverage`. Full suite not needed (no shared code).
- Browser: local server on a copy of `scheduler.db`, test engineer: upload a report on a TSR, revise that TSR, Save
  Final Report again → success, card "Uploaded", row on My Calibrations; clean console. Remove the DB copy, test
  account and temporary launch entries afterwards.

## After implementation

- Self-review the diff; confirm `upload_online_tsr_attachment`, `record_calibration_report_upload`,
  `submit_calibration_certificate_for_submission`, `revise_online_tsr_submission` and the My Calibrations routes still
  work (no function, id or handler removed or renamed).
- Prove the new tests fail without the change, run the focused modules, browser check, `releases.json`, `changes.md`,
  update Status here.

  other dirty files, or other sessions' uncommitted plans/log lines); verify `origin/main` and Railway deployment
  metadata.

## Risks

- History: the older revision no longer lists the report; it now belongs to the latest revision (same file, not
  duplicated).
- An older `Pending` certificate becomes `Superseded` — existing behaviour whenever a newer certificate is sent.
- Blast radius: only Calibration Report uploads; ordinary attachments and approved-report rules unchanged.

## Context

The 2026-10-15 page scan and design scan of Product Inventory (`templates/products.html` in product mode,
`/products_page`; Impeccable critique 24/40, snapshot `.impeccable/critique/2026-10-15T05-22-36Z__templates-products-html.md`).
The scan found that CSV Import silently erases owner and dates, Export is broken for engineers, and the server accepts bad
dates and unknown clients; the critique found dark-theme contrast failures, a modal taller than the screen and red status
badges on half the rows. The same template also renders Genoray (`/genoray`) and Vieworks (`/vieworks`); those pages

## Decisions taken (owner, 2026-10-15)

## Investigation

- **Import erases fields** (`import_products`, `app.py:66737`): for an existing product it always assigns `room`,
  `client_id`, `start_warranty_date`, `end_warranty_date`, `bsid` (`app.py:66817-66824`), even when the CSV has no such
  column (`csv_get` returns empty). Repro on a DB copy: CSV with only Serial Number + Description → MPF16C78B011 lost its
  owner and both dates. Contract already follows the "column present" rule (`has_contract_column`).
- **Import does not uppercase serials** (`app.py:66778`), while `add_product` (`:64594`) and `update_product` (`:64825`)
  do. Importing `zzscan6` beside `ZZSCAN6` made a second row (PK is case-sensitive in SQLite).
- **Import owner matching** `csv_find_client_id` (`app.py:66586`) falls back to a 0.75 similarity match and applies it
  silently. The exported "N/A" owner is also counted as "unmatched" on re-import (`export_products`, `app.py:55505`).
- **Add/Edit accept bad input** (`add_product` `:64573`, `update_product` `:64789`): `parse_date` (`:7747`) turns an
  unreadable date into `None` without an error; no end-before-start check (the P.O. route has one, `:64762`); `client_id`
  is not checked against `Client` (999999 saved, shows "N/A"); a 307-character serial was saved (column is 100).
- **Export button** is shown to everyone (`products.html:51`), but `/export_products` is `is_admin_authorized()` only
  (`app.py:55495`): an engineer lands on raw `{"message":"Denied"}`. Genoray/Vieworks exports allow everyone with page
  access (`app.py:66156`, `:66523`), so the button must stay for those modes.
- **Delete of a missing serial** returns 200 `success` (`app.py:65043-65075`).
- **Save double-click** (`saveProduct`, `products.html:2044`): no busy guard; the second Add POST returns 409 and the
  page shows "Database Error: Serial number … already exists" after the success toast. Every failure message is prefixed
  "Database Error:" (`:2153`), including validation messages.

- **Unused route** `/get_products_summary` (`app.py:34729`): no caller in templates, static JS or tests.

# Late Calibration Report — real upload failure reason and automatic retry (1 batch)

**Status:** Executed (2026-10-15, on "Execute the late upload retry plan."). Published on "commit and push. never db and dirty" as `70ae4b5` on `main`, together with the certificate-result plan below (service worker v327).

### Amendments during execution

- **Not client-side only:** `app.py` gained `calibration_submit_failure_message(code, message)`, now used by both
  `record_calibration_submit_failure` and `calibration_upload_certificate_payload`, so the Save Final Report notice and
  My Calibrations word a certificate failure the same way (the upload reply said only "Certificate No." where My
  Calibrations said "Missing values: Certificate No.").
- **Notices go to the visible place:** the calibration script's `showStatus` writes into the editor's own status box
  (`hostId:'calibration-report-modal-status'`), which is hidden once the editor closes — so a success notice shown
  before `close()`, or during a retry with the editor closed, was invisible. New `showLateUploadStatus` uses the editor
  box only while `#calibration-report-overlay` is open, else the page notices; `finishLateUpload` now closes the editor
  first and then shows the result.
- **One notice slot:** every late-upload notice (recovered, retrying, failed, uploaded) and the page-load notice when a
  retry is starting share `replaceKey:'late-calibration-upload'`, so the newest replaces the older ones. Without it the
  browser check showed "It is still not uploaded" and "Retry Save Final Report…" after the report had already uploaded.
  The page-load notice now reads "Calibration Report saved on this device is uploading again now." when a retry starts.
- **Tests** went into `tests/test_calibration_late_upload_feedback.py` (Node vm with fake timers, plus source checks)
  rather than `test_tsr_calibration_report.py`; the pinned `saveFinalReport` contract there now checks
  `finishLateUpload(lateResult)`. Node output is read as UTF-8 (the em dash broke on the Windows code page).
- **Fail-without-fix proof:** all 8 new retry tests failed on the code before the change.
- **Browser (DB copy, test engineer, three TSRs, real Save Final Report with the local server stopped):** notice "The
  connection dropped during the upload. It will upload automatically when the connection is back."; after restarting
  the server the timed retry uploaded (`POST /upload_online_tsr_attachment` 200, card "Uploaded", row on My
  Calibrations); after closing and reopening the page the upload restarted within seconds and the page ended on one
  current notice ("uploaded, but the certificate was not sent: Missing values…" with Open My Calibrations — the copy's
  test machine has no BSID). 375 px: scrollWidth 375, notices wrap inside the screen. Console errors were only the
  deliberate refused connections while the server was down.
- **Seen, not changed:** while the server is down the editor's autosave line also says "Calibration Report could not
  be saved. Keep this page open and try again." (account-backup status, `app-calibration-report.js:422`), next to the
  new "saved on this device" notice. One My Calibrations read made right after an upload did not list the new row; a
  read a few seconds later did. Neither was part of this plan.

## Context

An engineer reported "Calibration Report saved locally but not uploaded" while on Wi-Fi with a low signal. On a weak
link the late upload (Save Final Report on an already-saved TSR) times out or drops; the screen then says "Retry Save
Final Report when you are online" although the device is online, the real reason is discarded, and the report waits on
the device until the engineer reopens the calibration-report page and presses Save Final Report again. Intended outcome:
the engineer sees the real reason, and the upload retries by itself when the connection allows.

## Decisions taken (owner, 2026-10-15)

- Show the real failure reason instead of "when you are online".
- Retry the late Calibration Report upload automatically when the connection is back.
- One batch; the previous plan (certificate result after Save Final Report) is the base this builds on.

## Investigation

- `saveStandaloneCalibrationReport` (`templates/offline_tsr.html:8108`): every failure — `navigator.onLine` false, any
  error thrown by `fetchTSRSyncJSON`, or a non-success JSON (except `calibration_report_already_uploaded`) — goes to
  `saveLocallyAfterFailure` (`:8146`), which returns `{status:'local_saved', upload_error:<message>}` and drops the error
  code and `retryable` flag.
- The caller ignores `upload_error` and shows fixed text (`static/js/app-calibration-report.js:1713`).
- `fetchTSRSyncJSON` (`templates/offline_tsr.html:942`) already classifies failures: `timeout` (AbortError),
  `network_error`, `session_expired` (redirect to `/login`, `requiresLogin`), `http_<status>` with `retryable` true for
  408/425/429/5xx or when the server says so.
- Upload timeout is fixed at 120 s (`templates/offline_tsr.html:8202`) regardless of the DOCX size.
- Nothing retries: the `online` listener at `templates/offline_tsr.html:5568` only re-sends the account backup
  (`/save_calibration_report_draft`), not the upload; the offline TSR queue (`scheduleOfflineTSRAutoSync`, `:8908`) never
  reads late reports; reopening the page restores the device copy (`restoreStandaloneLateCalibrationDraft`, `:5588`)
  with a warning but does not upload.
- Retry is safe: the server treats the same `attachment_token` as a duplicate (existing-file branch of
  `upload_online_tsr_attachment`, `app.py` ~27175) and returns success; if the timed-out upload actually landed, the
  retry simply confirms it.
- `_late_calibration_report_pending` is set on every late draft (`prepareStandaloneLateCalibrationDraft`, `:3764`), so on
  reopen it cannot tell "Save Final Report was pressed and failed" from ordinary edits — a separate marker is needed.
- An account-restored copy (`candidate.source === 'account'`) has no DOCX blob on the device; only a device copy with a
  resolvable blob can be retried without regenerating.

## Execution steps

1. **`saveStandaloneCalibrationReport` keeps the failure details** (`templates/offline_tsr.html`): `saveLocallyAfterFailure`
   also returns `upload_error_code`, `retryable`, `requires_login` (from the thrown error; `offline` → code `offline`,
   retryable), and sets `_late_calibration_report_upload_failed: true` on `latePayload` before the device save (the copy
   is deleted on successful upload, so the marker goes with it). Done: result carries the code; device copy carries the
   marker.
2. **Size-aware timeout** (same function): `timeoutMs = min(600000, max(120000, Math.ceil(blob.size / 20480) * 1000))`.
   Done: the fixed `timeoutMs:120000` is gone from this call.
3. **One reason mapper** in `static/js/app-calibration-report.js`: `describeLateUploadFailure(result)` → `{ reason,
   autoRetry }`, exposed as `window.calibrationReport.describeUploadFailure`:
   - `timeout` → "The upload timed out — the connection is too weak or slow." (retry)
   - `network_error` / `offline` → "The connection dropped during the upload." (retry)
   - `session_expired` / `http_401` / `requires_login` → "Your session expired. Sign in again, then press Save Final
     Report." (no retry)
   - `http_5xx` or `retryable` → "The server could not take the upload: <message>." (retry)
   - other `http_4xx` → the server's message (no retry).
   Done: pure function, no DOM access.
4. **`finishLateUpload(lateResult)`** in `app-calibration-report.js`: moves the current success branch of
   `saveFinalReport` (`markUploaded`, the certificate-result message, `renderCard()`, `close()`) into one function used by
   both Save Final Report and the retry. Done: no duplicated success handling.
5. **Failure message** (`saveFinalReport`, `local_saved` branch): "Calibration Report saved on this device but not
   uploaded: <reason>" + " It will upload automatically when the connection is back." when `autoRetry`, otherwise
   nothing more (the reason says what to do). Done: the "when you are online" text is gone.
6. **Automatic retry while the page is open** (`app-calibration-report.js`): `scheduleLateUploadRetry()` — backoff 30 s,
   60 s, 120 s, then every 300 s; plus an immediate attempt on `window` `online`. Each attempt calls
   `window.saveStandaloneCalibrationReport()` with the already-generated report (no `preparePayload` / regeneration); a
   busy flag shared with `saveFinalReport` prevents overlap; the retry stops on success (→ `finishLateUpload`), on a
   non-retryable failure (→ failure message, no reschedule), or when the engineer saves, removes or clears the report.
   One short "Retrying the Calibration Report upload…" info status per attempt. Done: timer and listener cleared on
   every stop path.
7. **Resume after reopening** (`restoreStandaloneLateCalibrationDraft`, `templates/offline_tsr.html:5588`): when the
   restored device copy has `_late_calibration_report_upload_failed` and its attachment blob resolves, call
   `window.calibrationReport.scheduleLateUploadRetry({ immediate:true })` after `apply`. Account-restored copies are left
   to the manual Save Final Report. Done: reopened failed uploads retry by themselves.
8. **Release:** `app-calibration-report.js?v=50` in `templates/offline_tsr.html`, `templates/calibration_center.html`, the
   service worker precache list in `app.py`, and the version pins in `tests/test_tsr_calibration_report.py` /
   `tests/test_calibration_center.py`; service worker `CACHE_VERSION` v327; `static/changelog/releases.json` item;
   `changes.md`; this plan's Status.

## Deliberately excluded

- Background upload after the page is closed (offline TSR queue / Create TSR pages): that needs building the upload
  outside the calibration editor; a larger change. Reopening the page covers it (step 7).
- No server change: duplicate-token handling already makes retries safe.
- No change to the account backup flow or the normal TSR save/sync path.

# Late Calibration Report — show the certificate result after Save Final Report (1 batch)

**Status:** Executed (2026-10-15, on "Execute the Late Calibration Report plan."). Published as `70ae4b5` on `main` with the retry plan above.

### Amendments during execution

- **Script cache-bust:** `app-calibration-report.js` is loaded with `?v=48` (`templates/offline_tsr.html`,
  `templates/calibration_center.html`, service worker precache list in `app.py`); bumped to `?v=49`, otherwise browsers
  keep the old script. Pins updated in `tests/test_tsr_calibration_report.py` and `tests/test_calibration_center.py`.
  Service worker v326-late-calibration-feedback.
- **Pinned text:** `test_calibration_only_final_save_uses_page_upload_without_normal_tsr_save` pinned the old success
  text "No new TSR revision was created."; it now pins "Calibration Report uploaded and sent to the approver."
- **Card note:** the "Certificate not sent" branch skips `queued`, `not_ready` and `superseded`; it sits after the BSID
  and temporary-model checks, so those notes still win.
- **Fail-without-fix proof:** before the fix, the failure-reason test errored (`KeyError: 'message'` on the retry path),
  the no-approver test failed (`'Pending' != 'awaiting_route'`) and the JS source test failed; the with-approver test is a
  coverage test and passes on both.
- **Browser (DB copy, test engineer, TSR 35):** the calibration-report page loads `app-calibration-report.js?v=49` in
  calibration-only mode with no console errors; Save Final Report still runs its validation ("Complete the Calibration
  Report…"). The three upload messages were **not** clicked through in the browser: that needs a fully filled report
  (equipment, dates, test tool, X-ray pages); they are covered by the route tests and the JS source test.

## Context

An engineer reported: TSR created, saved and sent to the client; then a Calibration Report was added and
**Save Final Report** clicked; the report "does not show in my calibration page as pending / for approval / sent to
approver". Reproduced on a scratch DB (2026-10-15): the late upload succeeds and the row does appear on My Calibrations
(`/calibration-center`), but as **Failed to send** with a reason (in the repro: equipment name/model not in the
catalog). The engineer was told "Calibration Report uploaded to the existing TSR. No new TSR revision was created." — a
plain success — so they believe it went to the approver. Intended outcome: after Save Final Report the engineer sees
whether the certificate was sent to the approver, and if not, why and where to fix it.

## Decisions taken (owner, 2026-10-15)

- Fix the feedback, not the workflow: show the certificate result (sent / failed reason / no approver) instead of the
  plain success message.
- One batch.

## Investigation

- The late upload (`upload_online_tsr_attachment`, `app.py:27028`) calls `submit_calibration_certificate_for_submission`
  straight after storing the DOCX (`app.py:27308`; retry/duplicate path `app.py:27195`). On failure it records
  `CALIBRATION_SUBMIT_FAILURE_MARKER`, which My Calibrations shows as "Failed to send" (`my_calibration_status`,
  `app.py:25360`).
- New-upload response `certificate` = approval dict on success, else `{'status': code, 'message': message}`
  (`app.py:27330`). Duplicate/retry response sends only `{'status': code}` — **no message** (`app.py:27215`).
- No approver assigned: the approval is still created as `Pending`; the response does not say no approver will get it.
  Only `get_calibration_certificate_status` derives "Awaiting approver assignment" (`app.py:26666`); My Calibrations
  shows it as Failed with `MY_CALIBRATION_NO_APPROVER_REASON`.
- Client: `saveStandaloneCalibrationReport` (`templates/offline_tsr.html:8108`) returns the upload JSON. The caller in
  `static/js/app-calibration-report.js:1708-1723` (calibration-only mode) calls `markUploaded(lateResult)` and always
  shows the fixed success text at line 1720. `markUploaded` (`:1604`) stores `result.certificate.status` and
  `error`, not `message`.
- Card note (`renderCard`, `:1754-1766`): unknown status codes such as `catalog_validation` / `missing_values` fall
  through to "Certificate queued until TSR sync." — also misleading after an upload. Known keys: `pending`,
  `awaiting_route` / `awaiting_approver_assignment`, `returned`, `approved`, `error` / `retryable`.
- Not the cause: page query (`_my_calibration_rows`, `app.py:25386`) correctly picks up late uploads because
  `record_calibration_report_upload` writes the top-level `_generated_calibration_report` marker (`app.py:27023`).
- Other ways a report is missing from the page entirely (not fixed here): upload failed/offline → saved on the device
  only, already warned ("saved locally but not uploaded", `:1713`); report saved from the normal TSR editor rather than
  calibration-only mode → local draft until TSR sync (`:1731`).

## Execution steps

1. **`app.py` — one helper, both responses.** Add `calibration_upload_certificate_payload(certificate_result, submission)`
   next to `record_calibration_report_upload`. Returns:
   - success with approval → `calibration_certificate_approval_to_dict(approval)`, and when `approval.status == 'Pending'`
     and `get_assigned_approvers_for_requester(submission.submitted_by_user_id, 'calibration_certificate')` is empty, its
     `status` set to `'awaiting_route'`;
   - otherwise → `{'status': code or 'not_requested', 'message': message or ''}`.
   Use it in both `jsonify` responses of `upload_online_tsr_attachment` (`:27215` and `:27330`). Done: both responses
   come from the helper; no other route changed.
2. **`markUploaded`** (`static/js/app-calibration-report.js:1604`): store
   `error: result.certificate.message || result.certificate.error || ''`. Done: failure reason kept in
   `state.certificate_approval.error`.
3. **Late upload message** (`:1718-1722`): after `markUploaded`, choose from `state.certificate_approval`:
   - `pending` → success "Calibration Report uploaded and sent to the approver.";
   - `awaiting_route` → warning "Calibration Report uploaded, but no approver is assigned to you. Contact admin.";
   - anything else (failure code) → warning "Calibration Report uploaded, but the certificate was not sent: <reason>"
     with `action:{ label:'Open My Calibrations', onClick: go to '/calibration-center' }` (the `showStatus` action option
     already used at `:1732`).
   Keep `renderCard()` and `close()` as now. Done: the fixed text at `:1720` is gone; the three messages exist.
4. **Card note** (`renderCard`, `:1762-1763`): add a branch — a status that is not one of the known keys and has
   `cert.error` → "Certificate not sent: <error>". Done: `catalog_validation` with a message no longer reads "queued
   until TSR sync".
5. **Release:** bump service worker `CACHE_VERSION` (`app.py:27943`, next vNN with label e.g.
   `late-calibration-feedback`); add a "Calibration Report save feedback" item to `static/changelog/releases.json`;
   `changes.md` entry; this plan's Status → In progress / Executed.

## Deliberately excluded

- Offline queue sync / normal TSR save paths (`templates/offline_tsr.html:8652`, `:9097`): their certificate result
  comes through TSR sync, a separate flow. Follow-up only if wanted.
- No change to certificate validation, catalog matching, approver routing, or My Calibrations statuses — they are
  already correct.
- No automatic retry; the existing Retry on My Calibrations stays the way to resend.

## Verification

- New `tests/test_calibration_late_upload_feedback.py` (fixture modelled on `_make_late_upload_fixture` in
  `tests/test_tsr_sync_reliability.py`, with `submitted_by_user_id` set; patch `managed_storage_write_bytes`,
  `schedule_calibration_report_conversion`, `can_work_on_existing_schedule_shift`):
  - patched submit failure with a message → response `certificate` has code + message, on the new-upload path **and**
    the same-token retry path;
  - patched submit success with a Pending approval, no approver assigned → `certificate.status == 'awaiting_route'`;
  - same with an approver assigned → `certificate.status == 'Pending'`;
  - JS source check: the three messages and the `/calibration-center` action exist, the old fixed text does not.
- Positive control: the route tests must fail on the current code (retry path has no message; no `awaiting_route`).
- Focused modules: the new file, `test_my_calibrations`, `test_tsr_sync_reliability`,
  `test_calibration_report_returned_fix`, `sw_cache_version` check. Full suite not needed (no shared code).
- Browser: local server on a copy of `scheduler.db`; test engineer with no approver → save a TSR, then Save Final Report
  from the calibration-report page → warning shown; assign an approver, repeat on a second TSR → "sent to the
  approver"; a report with a non-catalog model → "not sent: <reason>" with Open My Calibrations working. 375 px, tap
  targets ≥44px, clean console. Remove the DB copy, test accounts and temporary launch entries afterwards.

## After implementation

- Self-review the diff; confirm `markUploaded`, `renderCard`, `showStatus`, `saveStandaloneCalibrationReport` and
  `upload_online_tsr_attachment` callers still work (no function, id or handler removed or renamed).
- Prove the new tests fail without the fix, run the focused modules, browser check, service worker bump,
  `releases.json`, `changes.md`, update Status here.
- Commit only the intended files on "commit and push" (never `scheduler.db`, `output/`, `tmp/`, handoffs or other dirty
  files); verify `origin/main` and Railway deployment metadata.

## Risks

  and the certificate is still created exactly as before.
